card.summary: A monthly allowance that renews forever: '25,000 GB-seconds' of Function execution, '900 GB-minutes' of AppSail container runtime, '2 GB-days' of Data Store ...

free_tier.stated: A monthly allowance that renews forever: '25,000 GB-seconds' of Function execution, '900 GB-minutes' of AppSail container runtime, '2 GB-days' of Data Store storage, '1,000,000' LLM input tokens and '500,000' LLM output tokens through QuickML, '1,800 CPU-seconds' of model training, '100,000' API Gateway requests and '300,000' Web Client Hosting requests. The page says: 'your free tier usage limits will be renewed every month forever'. Signing up also gives 'USD 250 in credits' as 'additional runway for 6 months'.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: The perpetual function allowance plus the 6-month USD 250 wallet is the useful pair: the credits can carry a burst build while the monthly free tier keeps a scheduled job alive after the credits end, and QuickML's 1M input tokens a month is a second, separate inference lane that survives the credit expiry.

limits.value: The container lane is the real ceiling: 900 GB-minutes a month is 15 GB-hours, so one always-on 1 GiB AppSail container runs about 15 hours a month before the free tier is spent; the per-request counters (1,000 Cache GET, 1,000 queries) bind long before any byte quota does.

record.limits_note: The container lane is the real ceiling: 900 GB-minutes a month is 15 GB-hours, so one always-on 1 GiB AppSail container runs about 15 hours a month before the free tier is spent; the per-request counters (1,000 Cache GET, 1,000 queries) bind long before any byte quota does.
record.binding_note: The container lane is the real ceiling: 900 GB-minutes a month is 15 GB-hours, so one always-on 1 GiB AppSail container runs about 15 hours a month before the free tier is spent; the per-request counters (1,000 Cache GET, 1,000 queries) bind long before any byte quota does.

evidence.proved: the pricing table row by row: 'Functions | Function execution | $0.000016 / GB-second | 25,000 GB-seconds', 'AppSail | Container runtime | $0.0013 / GB-minute | 900 GB-minutes', 'QuickML | LLM input tokens | $0.20 / million tokens | 1,000,000 tokens', 'Model training: CPU | $0.0004 / vCPU-second | 1,800 CPU-seconds', quoted

the page description reads 'With a free tier that renews every month and $250 in credits to explore for your first six months'; the body reads 'your free tier usage limits will be renewed every month forever', quoted

'the free tier allowance is only available with the pay-as-you-go pricing model', the allowance is account-wide rather than per project, and 'The free tier allowance is refreshed monthly, and is not just a one-time benefit', quoted
'Catalyst offers 25k GB-seconds of Serverless Function requests, 2 GB storage in the Data Store, 1000 GET requests in Cache', quoted, matching the pricing table
Catalyst documents a REST API beside its CLI and SDKs

record.notes: India's strongest reachable free tier in verification because the door is a Zoho account rather than an Aadhaar or a GST number, and nothing on the free-tier page asks for a card. The catch is arithmetic, not policy: GB-minute and GB-second billing means a 512 MiB container gets twice the wall-clock hours of a 1 GiB one, and the free tier is spent by concurrency, not by month. Not probed: whether an Indian or non-Indian signup is treated differently, and whether the pay-as-you-go model needs a card on file. Both would need a signup.

record.provider: Zoho Mail Free — 5 GB/user, up to 25 users via referral, live IMAP

free_tier.stated: Zoho's own help: "Each user is allocated 5 GB of storage under the free plan." Headcount: free plan is 5 users in select regions, expandable. Press release "increasing the number of mailboxes offered with the Zoho Mail free email hosting plan, doubling it from five to ten users .. extend the free user limit to 25 users by simply referring other customers".

record.tooling: IMAP probe-verified: `imap.zoho.com:993` -> `* OK svwall.zoho.com IMAP4 Server` / `* CAPABILITY IMAP4rev1 ... ESEARCH LIST-EXTENDED LIST-STATUS WITHIN LITERAL- ACL CONDSTORE`. Attachments: 30 MB normal, "Huge Attachment" up to 1 GB (link-based, not stored in the mailbox).
record.chaining: 5 GB × 25 users = 125 GB per free organisation, × N organisations. The referral ladder is the multiplier and it is free.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap 30 MB real attachment (the 1 GB 'Huge Attachment' is a link, so it does not consume mailbox quota. It is not storage). 5 GB/user is the byte ceiling. Free plan is geo-restricted: "currently available only in selected data centers and may not be accessible in all regions.".
record.reliability_note: Free and paid plans cannot be mixed in one org; upgrading one user can disable the rest. Free plan availability varies by data centre.

evidence.proved: "5 GB of storage under the free plan"
5 -> 10 users, extendable to 25 via referrals
probe: imap.zoho.com:993 -> * OK svwall.zoho.com IMAP4 Server + full CAPABILITY

record.notes: Zoho's own help: "Each user is allocated 5 GB of storage under the free plan." Headcount: free plan is 5 users in select regions, expandable. Press release "increasing the number of mailboxes offered with the Zoho Mail free email hosting plan, doubling it from five to ten users .. extend the free user limit to 25 users by simply referring other customers".

dead_end.why: Zoho's own help: "Each user is allocated 5 GB of storage under the free plan." Headcount: free plan is 5 users in select regions, expandable — press release "increasing the number of mailboxes offered with the Zoho Mail free email hosting plan, doubling it from five to ten users ... extend the free user limit to 25 users by simply referring other customers".
